title: A general framework for crystallization in maximal hard-core models
authors: Alexander Barg, Qidong He, Geyang Wang
abstract: We study general maximal hard-core models on periodic lattice-type graphs. While for standard models, phase coexistence may arise for high activity, for maximal models this behavior may occur also for sufficiently low activity values. Relying on the concept of volume allocation, we develop a {\em unified set of assumptions} that imply the Peierls condition, a convergent cluster expansion for the partition function, and hence the conclusions of Pirogov-Sinai theory for this class of models. We further check these assumptions for a number of examples including standard lattice-type periodic graphs, proving crystallization for both high and low activity. We also derive estimates for the values of activity that bound the phase coexistence regions in the phase diagram, rewriting for this purpose the proof of a technical result in the derivation of Pirogov-Sinai theory.
summary: This paper introduces a general mathematical framework to analyze phase transitions and crystallization in maximal hard-core lattice models. By developing a concept of 'volume allocation,' the authors successfully extend the applicability of the powerful Pirogov-Sinai theory to regimes previously inaccessible, proving crystallization for various lattice types. This provides a powerful theoretical tool for understanding ordered phases in constrained physical systems.
main_problem: Developing a general mathematical framework to study phase coexistence and prove crystallization in maximal hard-core lattice models, especially in regimes where standard methods fail.
main_result: The authors establish a unified set of assumptions, based on volume allocation, that allow the application of Pirogov-Sinai theory to prove crystallization for maximal hard-core models at both high and low activity levels.
method: The methodology heavily relies on adapting the concept of volume allocation (from Zahradn´ık's contour formalism) to the constraints of maximal configurations, leading to necessary conditions for the Peierls argument.
model_or_system: The system is a maximal hard-core model defined on periodic lattice-type graphs (e.g., $\mathbb{Z}^d$, triangular, honeycomb). The model is governed by a Hamiltonian involving chemical potentials ($\mu_x$) associated with placed tiles.
key_observables: Phase coexistence, crystallization, allocated volume $v(x | X)$, and the existence of perfect configurations.
important_parameters: Activity/Chemical Potentials ($\mu_x$), inverse temperature ($ eta$), and the dimensionality/lattice structure ($d$).
main_assumptions: The framework requires assuming the existence of a volume allocation satisfying specific local and global optimization conditions (Assumptions 1 and 2) to apply Pirogov-Sinai theory.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the coordinate realizations of lattices ($A_2, H_2$), the discrete volume allocation on $\mathbb{Z}^2$, and the concept of supercells on the honeycomb lattice.
paper_structure: The paper builds from defining the general maximal hard-core model, introducing the volume allocation concept, proving key lemmas relating perfect configurations to periodic ground states, and finally applying these results to prove crystallization in various lattice settings.
why_interesting: While focused on classical statistical mechanics, the rigorous mathematical machinery involving volume allocation and phase transition theory (Pirogov-Sinai) is highly relevant for understanding phase transitions in quantum many-body systems, especially those involving geometric constraints or local interactions.
